analysis: The PR is documentation only. The new 'Provider cache storage' section in encryption.md (head lines ~176-240) describes a configurable SSD cache payload directory (`darkbloom cache set --directory`) for local or external APFS volumes, with a filesystem-UUID pin and descriptor-based revalidation. It also covers keys staying in the SE/Keychain, DBK3 format unchanged, and a persistent write ledger kept on the Mac. The section itself admits residuals: ciphertext and metadata persist on detached media past TTL, TTL deletion needs the volume mounted, restart freshness comes from mtimes (replay is possible), UUID cloning defeats the pin, and a malicious controller can lie or retain data. Relevant IDs: T-041 (at-rest TTL/LRU/kv3-root claims), T-016, A-001, A-003, ADV-001. T-041 has not been updated to match, and that is the one finding. cache-aware-routing.md is shown as head text only (lines 911-1231, no patch), so the actual diff is not visible. Nothing in the visible text raises a security regression: cache scope remains coordinator-authored HMAC, routing is off by default, and no telemetry exports scope or prefix hashes. Source code for CacheVolume.swift, CacheStorage.swift and SSDNoFollowIO.swift was not supplied, so the claimed validation (UUID pin, ownership, symlink refusal, descriptor-based I/O) is unverified. Later passes should check those files if present, and check that provider config changes do not let a symlink or mount swap redirect plaintext or cache writes.

findings.detail: The new section documents `darkbloom cache set --directory`, which can put DBK3 payloads on an external APFS volume. It also admits that TTL/LRU deletion needs the volume mounted. Detached or inaccessible media can keep ciphertext and metadata indefinitely, and switching locations leaves old ciphertext behind. Restart freshness is seeded from mtimes, so a malicious disk can replay valid files and metadata. A filesystem-UUID pin can be defeated by cloning the UUID. T-041 and its mitigations still say the at-rest window is bounded by a 30-minute sliding TTL and a box-wide LRU budget. They name `darkbloom/kv3` as the only on-disk root, and describe KEK wipe as the purge. Nothing in them covers an operator-chosen, possibly removable store. A malicious operator or enclosure controller retains ciphertext plus visible size, time and model metadata past the TTL (ADV-001). It can also replay still-valid files. Fix: update T-041 to add the selectable volume as a new at-rest surface with these residuals. Reword the TTL and LRU mitigations as 'while mounted'. Add the UUID-pin limitation and make the KEK wipe the only guaranteed purge. Add the cache-volume files named in the PR to its detection_hint and affected_files.
findings.title: T-041 at-rest window and purge claims do not cover relocatable or external cache volumes
